## Paper

Algorithmic collusion with imperfect monitoring

## World

pricing_arena

## Institution

Demand shock / imperfect monitoring variant.

## Agent type

Learning pricing firms.

## Theoretical benchmark

Collusion under noisy monitoring and punishment/price-war dynamics.

## Learning setup

Repeated pricing where the signal mapping from actions to rewards is noisier or institutionally perturbed.

## Metrics

Collusion, price dispersion, profit, exploitability, robustness under shock.

## Main result

Q-learning algorithms can autonomously learn to collude in an environment with imperfect monitoring without being instructed to do so, and without communication. Collusion is sustained by punishments in the form of price wars triggered by deviations and adverse demand shocks.

## What they prove

Q-learning algorithms can learn to collude in an environment with imperfect monitoring without communication, and punishments are triggered by deviations and adverse demand shocks.

## What they only simulate

The impact of imperfect monitoring on collusion is simulated, but not formally proven.

## What they do NOT test

The robustness of results to changes in modeling choices is not tested.

## What we need to reproduce

Treat demand shocks as an information/monitoring change and compare whether collusion/exploitability survive under the shock.

## How our project differs

The paper focuses on imperfect monitoring in algorithmic collusion. This repo uses the demand_shock mechanism as a coarse monitoring/environment stress test.

## Implementation obligations

Explicit demand_shock mechanism; fixed seeds; same metrics as baseline pricing; robustness comparison against no-institution pricing.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

demand_shock rows in outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv and exploitability summaries.

## Failure modes to audit

Calling random noise an institution without documenting the information channel; comparing shocked and unshocked runs with different training protocols; ignoring variance/dispersion.

## Project code comparison

Compare Algorithmic collusion with imperfect monitoring to the demand_shock mechanism and pricing outputs. The repo should describe this as a monitoring stress test, not as a full reproduction of the paper's model.
